newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said Thursday its policy-making council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting, in line with market expectations.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at 3 percent.

Financial markets had been confident in advance of the meeting that there would be no surprise policy changes from the central bank at this week's meeting after it slashed its repo rate to 3 percent from 3.30 percent just two weeks ago.
German growth data released Thursday also showed little economic need for a further easing.

The German statistics office said that the economy grew more strongly than expected in the second quarter, expanding 1.5 percent from the first quarter and 1.2 percent in the second quarter compared with a year earlier.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had made clear in a statement soon after the rate cut announcement that markets should not expect any further policy moves for some time.
German bond and share markets showed little response to the Bundesbank decision. Shares were trading slightly lower while the bond market held moderate morning gains.
